thread.title_full: Medicaid COVID-19 services in Sunrise result in at least $9,196 in 2024 payments

author: N. K. Reynolds
title: Medicaid COVID-19 services in Sunrise result in at least $9,196 in 2024 payments
text:
At least $9,196 in Medicaid payments were made in Sunrise in 2024 for services billed with HCPCS codes specifically linked to COVID-19, based on records from the U.S. Department of Health and Human Services Medicaid Provider Spending database.
Medicaid, a public insurance program managed by states and funded together by federal and state governments, provides coverage for low-income people, families, seniors, children, and individuals with disabilities. The program forms a significant part of the nation’s health care system.
Since taxpayer dollars support Medicaid, fluctuations in local billing help illustrate how public health care resources are distributed within a community.
This report identified COVID-19 services through HCPCS codes designated as “COVID-19” or “coronavirus” within billing details or reference materials. Therefore, these numbers only represent services explicitly categorized as COVID-related and exclude other pandemic care billed under general or alternative codes.
In comparison, Miami led all Florida cities in Medicaid payments associated with COVID-19 services in 2024, with virus-related claims totaling $270,279.
Data indicates that My Clinical Lab Inc was the sole provider in Sunrise submitting Medicaid claims for COVID-19 services during 2024.
Total Medicaid payments across remaining claim groups rose by $10,008,352 from 2020 to 2024, which marks a 14.8% growth.
According to the Centers for Medicare & Medicaid Services, Medicaid spending by federal and state governments combined was about $871.7 billion in fiscal year 2023, or nearly 18% of national health spending, significantly higher than the approximately $613.5 billion spent in 2019, prior to the COVID-19 pandemic.
This change reflects an estimated 40% increase in just a few years, largely due to expanded enrollment and rising use during and following the pandemic.
Recent federal budget actions during the Trump administration have included legislative efforts to restrict federal Medicaid funding and modify the structure of the program. For example, the “One Big Beautiful Bill Act,” enacted in 2025, is forecast to reduce federal Medicaid spending by more than $1 trillion over 10 years and brings in measures such as work requirements and greater cost-sharing. These could decrease coverage and federal support for some recipients, shifting more expenses to states while Medicaid remains vital for millions.

|---|---|---|---|
| 2024 | $9,196 | -95.4% | $77,833,577 |
| 2023 | $201,629 | -97.2% | $84,830,798 |
| 2022 | $7,283,505 | 742% | $78,457,590 |
| 2021 | $865,032 | 664.5% | $65,618,931 |
| 2020 | $113,149 | N/A | $67,929,179 |
| 2019 | $0 | N/A | $102,753,880 |
| 2018 | $0 | N/A | $42,295,815 |
| HCPCS Code | Description | Medicaid Payments | Claims |
|---|---|---|---|
| 87635 | COVID Specific | $8,617 | 782 |
| 86769 | Immunoassay | $556 | 195 |
| 86328 | Immunoassay | $23 | 95 |
Note: Totals only include HCPCS codes specifically labeled for COVID-19 services and do not represent the full extent of pandemic-related health care expenditures.
The information in this report comes from the U.S. Department of Health and Human Services Medicaid Provider Spending database. Access the source data here.
